A real flesh-and-blood man, not a 3D render, not CGI, not a game character, not animation, not cartoon, not stylized illustration, not painterly art. Real human anatomy, real skin, real hair, real fabric, natural photographic depth of field, real camera grain and color. Documentary-grade realism throughout.

REFERENCE FACE
The character's face is taken directly from the supplied reference photos: adult male, mid-20s to early-30s, warm medium-bronze skin, dark wavy hair in the reference color, full dark mustache with a small soul-patch tuft under the lower lip, dark brown eyes, broad straight nose, soft rounded jaw, faint moles on the cheeks. The face, complexion, and facial features must match the reference 100% in every shot. Expression carries quiet menace: a slightly sullen, defiant glare, brows lightly furrowed, jaw set, hard confident stare.

FACE LOCK
Keep the reference man's face unchanged: same bone structure, same mustache and chin tuft, same eyes, nose, and lips, same complexion and moles. Adjust only the expression to a hard, sullen, defiant look with lightly furrowed brows — do not change the underlying features or proportions. The face is completely clean with absolutely no face paint, war paint, or cosmetic lines. Do not slim, age, or restyle the face. Keep the reference hair color, but the hair is longer than the reference and worn pulled back. Everything else about the face stays identical to the reference.

HAIR AND EARS
Long dark hair pulled back off the face and gathered into a single high bun/top-knot at the back of the head. Hair texture is loosely wavy, not tightly curly and not straight — soft natural waves with gentle bends. From the bun, long wavy strands fall down the back of the head and neck. The hair looks unwashed and lived-in: slightly greasy and oily at the roots, sweat-dampened, with a dull low sheen rather than clean bounce, a few stray flyaways. The hairline and forehead are clean and exposed, no hair hanging over the face. Both ears stay fully exposed and uncovered by hair. Ears are pierced and stretched, with clean, modern curved geometric polished horn or synthetic tusk ornaments hanging through the lobes instead of metal earrings.

CHARACTER DESIGN
An original dystopian or fantasy desert warrior: weathered post-apocalyptic look, raw survival presence. Hair long and wavy, unwashed and slightly greasy, pulled back into a single high bun with loose wavy strands falling behind, face and ears exposed. Simple primitive-futuristic accents only. No ethnic headdresses, no ceremonial plumes, no traditional indigenous items.

PHYSIQUE
Heavily muscled and powerfully built, in peak physical condition, dense lean working muscle on a medium-height frame. Strong, thick muscle mass with sharp, clearly defined relief across the whole body: large developed biceps and triceps, thick forearms, full square heavy pectorals, hard well-cut six-pack abdominals with pronounced obliques, broad thick shoulders and traps, muscular back, and strong powerful legs with defined quads and calves. Athletic, dense and imposing but still lean and flexible — a hardened fighter physique with low body fat and crisp muscle separation, clearly stronger and more muscular than an average man, not soft bodybuilder bulk and not skinny.

TATTOOS
Extensive, purely abstract geometric and sci-fi tech-inspired tattoos covering chest, stomach, the full back, both arms, and both legs front and back (thighs, shins, and calves). The style is entirely non-representational, mixing sharp vector linework, interlocking mathematical fractal patterns, and symmetrical circuit-board logic. Roughly 40% of the total body skin is covered in dense solid blackwork panels, while the rest transitions into fine stippled dotwork gradients and clean geometric grids. Both arms are fully sleeved from shoulder to wrist with no bare gaps. A single large centerpiece design dominates the back: a massive, highly detailed abstract fractal crest or interlocking geometric shield spanning between the shoulder blades down to the lower back, surrounded by complex circuit-like lines covering the rest of the back. No animals, no cultural symbols, no runes, and no tribal motifs are present.
The tattoos are rendered with absolute symmetry and sharp, clean precision, looking like professional modern graphic body art integrated into the skin, stretching naturally over the muscle relief. Consistent placement and design across all shots.

TATTOO CONTINUITY LOCK
The chest, neck, collarbone and upper-shoulder tattoos visible in the FRONT PORTRAIT (Shot 1) must be exactly the same design, placement, and pattern as the chest and shoulder tattoos in the FULL BODY FRONT (Shot 3). Same modern geometric motifs, same blackwork shapes, same clean fractal lines in both shots — the portrait and the full-body front view are the same body, so the overlapping tattooed areas match perfectly with no differences.

WARDROBE AND BODY
Bare torso, fully exposed muscular chest and stomach showing the tattoos and muscle relief. Legs are mostly bare and exposed below the garment, showing the front and back leg tattoos. Barefoot, no sandals, bare soles on the ground.
Groin garment is a wrapped-cloth loincloth — NOT fur and NOT tailored shorts. A long strip of canvas fabric wound and folded around the hips and between the legs, wrapping over the groin and the upper thighs so the covered area roughly matches the coverage of short shorts, while clearly reading as hand-wound draped fabric with visible folds, overlaps, and a knotted/tucked closure at the waist — not a sewn garment. The cloth is worn and weathered: frayed edges, loose threads, scattered dirt and dust stains, faded patchy color, and clearly pieced together from several mismatched scraps of fabric of slightly different earth tones and weaves stitched and tucked together. This wrap is the only garment. Modest coverage, nothing explicit. The face is completely clear of any paint or markings.

SKIN AND DETAIL
Hyper-realistic skin texture: visible pores, fine surface grain, subtle sheen of sweat on the shoulders and chest, sun-weathered roughness, faint natural tone variation across the body, the reference cheek moles preserved. A few old battle scars present — a pale healed slash across the ribs, a short scar on one forearm, a small mark on the brow — healed and natural, not bloody or fresh. Scars sit slightly raised or paler than surrounding skin. Skin reads as living tissue stretched over real working muscle, with natural creases at the joints.

FORMAT MODE
Single static character reference sheet, one consistent character, exactly four shots side by side, all the same person with identical reference face, hair bun, geometric ear ornaments, modern tattoos, scars, and cloth wrap.

FOUR SHOTS
Shot 1 — FRONT PORTRAIT: head-and-shoulders close-up, facing camera, hard sullen defiant glare with lightly furrowed brows, showing the reference face, clean skin with no paint, wavy hair pulled back into the high bun with loose wavy strands falling behind, exposed pierced ears with modern tusk ornaments, mustache, brow scar, and the geometric chest/shoulder tattoo that matches Shot 3.
Shot 2 — PROFILE PORTRAIT: head-and-shoulders close-up in full side profile (90° turn), set jaw and slightly furrowed brow, showing the nose-and-jaw profile line, the high bun and loose wavy strands falling at the back, the fully exposed ear with hanging modern tusk ornament, and clean facial skin from the side.
Shot 3 — FULL BODY FRONT: full figure head to bare feet, facing camera straight on, arms relaxed at sides, weight even, heavily muscled chest, six-pack stomach, fully sleeved muscular arms, defined leg muscles with front-of-leg modern geometric tattoos, clear muscle relief, chest/shoulder tattoos matching Shot 1, and the cloth wrap covering groin and upper thighs visible.
Shot 4 — FULL BODY BACK: full figure head to bare feet, back to camera, clearly showing the muscular tattooed back and shoulders, the high bun with falling wavy strands, the large abstract fractal shield centerpiece tattoo across the back, plus arm and back-of-leg geometric tattoos, and the rear of the wrapped cloth over the seat and upper thighs.
Shots 3 and 4 at identical scale, feet aligned on the same ground line.

OPTICS
Portrait shots (front and profile): 29° diagonal field of view, short telephoto portrait lens character, camera 4 to 6 meters, flattering stable face proportions, sharp subject, softly compressed background.
Full-body shots: 47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character, camera 3 to 5 meters, natural human-eye perspective, zero distortion, true body proportions, full figure sharp head to bare feet.

CAMERA
Eye-level, locked tripod, no movement, no perspective foreshortening. Even framing with equal headroom and floor space. Consistent subject height in both full-body shots and consistent head size in both portraits.

PHYSICS AND MATERIAL
The wrapped cloth hangs with real fabric weight, visible weave, layered folds and overlaps over the hips and upper thighs, frayed scrap edges catching the light, the waist knot pressing slightly into the skin. The high bun holds its shape while loose wavy strands fall behind with natural weight; the unwashed, slightly oily hair clumps in soft heavier locks rather than light fluffy curls. Geometric tusk ear ornaments hang with small weight. Tattoo ink sits flat on living skin and follows the curvature of the muscles across chest, stomach, arms, back and legs. Bare feet make full flat contact with the floor, toes spread under body weight. 

LIGHTING
Clean neutral studio key from front-upper-left with soft fill, even exposure across all four shots, gentle shadow under the feet. Realistic photographic light falloff and soft skin specular highlights that reveal the muscle relief. Reference skin tone, face, muscle definition, scars, tattoo black stay accurate and consistent. No dramatic shadow, no color cast — a flat readable reference sheet.

Built on the face of the supplied reference person. Neutral studio reference layout showing the same single character across four defined shots for identity locking.
REFERENCE FACE The character's face is taken directly from the supplied reference photos: adult male, mid-20s to early-30s, warm medium-bronze skin, dark hair with the same curl texture and color as the reference, full dark mustache with a small soul-patch tuft under the lower lip, dark brown eyes, broad straight nose, soft rounded jaw, calm neutral gaze, faint moles on the cheeks. The face, complexion, and facial features must match the reference 100% in every shot.
FACE LOCK Keep the reference man's face unchanged: same bone structure, same mustache and chin tuft, same eyes, nose, and lips, same complexion and moles. War paint sits on top of this face without changing its features. Do not slim, age, or restyle the face. Keep the reference hair color and curl texture, but the hair is longer than the reference and worn pulled back. Everything else about the face stays identical to the reference.
HAIR AND EARS Long dark curly hair gathered cleanly into a single bun/knot at the back of the head, pulled back off the face. No loose hair hanging over the face. Both ears are fully exposed, not covered by hair. Ears are pierced, and instead of metal earrings small carved bones are worn through the piercings as primitive ornaments.
CHARACTER DESIGN An original tribal warrior styled after an Australian Aboriginal bush hunter: weathered desert look, natural earth presence. Hair long and tied back in a single bun, ears exposed with bone piercings. Simple primitive accents only — bone or wood ornaments. No feathered headdress, no ceremonial plumes, no modern items.
PHYSIQUE Excellent athletic condition: lean, wiry, sinewy build with a dancer's flexibility, not bulky. Low body fat. Clearly defined abdominal muscles and a developed, well-built chest that read plainly. Strong shoulders and forearms, visible muscle separation, taut skin over working muscle. Powerful but supple — a body built for climbing, running, and hunting, not a bodybuilder.
TATTOOS Extensive tribal tattoos covering chest, stomach, both arms and both legs, mixing heavy blackwork (bold solid black panels and thick bands), dotwork (fine stippled gradients and shaded geometric fields), and rune-style linework drawn from Turkic and Celtic runic motifs — angular Turkic runiform marks combined with interlaced Celtic knotwork and looping rune bands. Roughly 40% of the total body skin is covered in dense solid blackwork, the rest is rune linework and dotwork shading. Both arms are fully sleeved from shoulder to wrist with no bare gaps. A single large centerpiece tattoo dominates the back: a big turtle with a patterned shell filled with rune-knotwork and dotwork, spanning between the shoulder blades down to the lower back. Abstract decorative patterns and runic motifs only, no readable modern letters. Consistent placement and design across all shots.
WARDROBE AND BODY Bare torso, fully exposed chest and stomach showing the tattoos. Legs are mostly bare and exposed below the garment. Barefoot, no sandals, bare soles on the ground. Groin garment is a wrapped-cloth loincloth — NOT fur and NOT tailored shorts. A long strip of fabric wound and folded around the hips and between the legs, wrapping over the groin and the upper thighs so the covered area roughly matches the coverage of short shorts, while clearly reading as hand-wound draped fabric with visible folds, overlaps, and a knotted/tucked closure at the waist — not a sewn garment. The cloth is worn and weathered: frayed edges, loose threads, scattered dirt and dust stains, faded patchy color, and clearly pieced together from several mismatched scraps of fabric of slightly different earth tones and weaves stitched and tucked together. This wrap is the only garment. Modest coverage, nothing explicit. Face carries war paint: simple horizontal battle stripes across the cheeks and one stripe over the nose bridge, in charcoal-black and ochre-red, slightly smudged like applied by hand — painted over the reference face without hiding its features.
SKIN AND DETAIL Hyper-realistic skin texture: visible pores, fine surface grain, subtle sheen of sweat on the shoulders and chest, sun-weathered roughness, faint natural tone variation across the body, the reference cheek moles preserved. A few old battle scars present — a pale healed slash across the ribs, a short scar on one forearm, a small mark on the brow — healed and natural, not bloody or fresh. Scars sit slightly raised or paler than surrounding skin. Skin reads as living tissue over real muscle, with natural creases at the joints.
FORMAT MODE Single static character reference sheet, one consistent character, exactly four shots side by side, all the same person with identical reference face, hair bun, bone ear ornaments, tattoos, scars, paint, and cloth wrap.
FOUR SHOTS Shot 1 — FRONT PORTRAIT: head-and-shoulders close-up, facing camera, showing the reference face, hair pulled back into the bun, exposed pierced ears with bone ornaments, mustache, war-paint stripes, brow scar, and the top of the chest tattoo. Shot 2 — PROFILE PORTRAIT: head-and-shoulders close-up in full side profile (90° turn), showing the nose-and-jaw profile line, the hair bun at the back, the fully exposed ear with bone piercing, and the war-paint stripes from the side. Shot 3 — FULL BODY FRONT: full figure head to bare feet, facing camera straight on, arms relaxed at sides, weight even, full chest, stomach, fully sleeved arms and leg tattoos, abs and chest definition, and the cloth wrap covering groin and upper thighs visible. Shot 4 — FULL BODY BACK: full figure head to bare feet, back to camera, clearly showing the hair bun, the large turtle centerpiece tattoo across the back, plus shoulder, arm and leg tattoos, and the rear of the wrapped cloth over the seat and upper thighs. Shots 3 and 4 at identical scale, feet aligned on the same ground line.
OPTICS Portrait shots (front and profile): 29° diagonal field of view, short telephoto portrait lens character, camera 4 to 6 meters, flattering stable face proportions, sharp subject, softly compressed background. Full-body shots: 47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character, camera 3 to 5 meters, natural human-eye perspective, zero distortion, true body proportions, full figure sharp head to bare feet.
CAMERA Eye-level, locked tripod, no movement, no perspective foreshortening. Even framing with equal headroom and floor space. Consistent subject height in both full-body shots and consistent head size in both portraits.
PHYSICS AND MATERIAL The wrapped cloth hangs with real fabric weight, visible weave, layered folds and overlaps over the hips and upper thighs, frayed scrap edges catching the light, the waist knot pressing slightly into the skin. Hair bun holds its shape with a few stray curls. Bone ear ornaments hang with small weight. Tattoo ink sits flat on living skin and follows muscle curvature across chest, stomach, arms, back and legs. Bare feet make full flat contact with the floor, toes spread under body weight. War paint reads as matte hand-applied pigment, not digital overlay.
LIGHTING Clean neutral studio key from front-upper-left with soft fill, even exposure across all four shots, gentle shadow under the feet. Reference skin tone, face, muscle definition, scars, tattoo black, and paint colors stay accurate and consistent. No dramatic shadow, no color cast — a flat readable reference sheet.
